# PCNE V9.1 — the two mappings, for the owner’s review

*Generated by `scripts/pcne-doc.ts` from `src/domain/pcne.ts` and `src/domain/pcne-maps.ts` (`npm run docs:pcne`). Do not edit by hand.*

**Status: DRAFT — waiting for the owner’s approval.** Until approved, every screen that shows a mapped box or category says it is a draft.

## Source

- The PCNE Classification V 9.1. Pharmaceutical Care Network Europe Association, © 2003–2020 (English edition, 2026). pcne.org. The codes and their English wording are copied from the official English document (PDF of 7 January 2026) and checked word for word against it; the Arabic lines in the app are PRECEPTOR’s explanations, not a PCNE translation.
- PCNE’s terms (from the document): “This classification may be used exclusively for Pharmaceutical Care Research and Practice, provided that the PCNE Association is informed of its use and of the results of any validations. Any use by commercial entities, or any use with a commercial purpose, is prohibited unless the user has obtained explicit permission from the PCNE Board. These conditions reflect PCNE’s long-standing policy and apply to both the current version and earlier versions of the classification. The exclusive place of jurisdiction for any dispute arising from the use of this classification is the District Court of The Hague, the Netherlands.”
- **Action for the department:** PCNE asks to be informed of the classification’s use (drp@pcne.org). PRECEPTOR is non-commercial teaching and practice; the department should send that notice. PRECEPTOR does not contact anyone.
- Cipolle categories: Cipolle RJ, Strand LM, Morley PC. Pharmaceutical Care Practice: The Patient-Centered Approach to Medication Management. 3rd ed. New York: McGraw-Hill; 2012. Only the category names are used.

## How codes combine

**Form boxes (Section 15, Section 8).** Each problem and cause code maps to one box. A card ticks the boxes of its causes; the box of its problem is added only when the causes give no box but “other” (or there is no cause). A code whose box is “other” writes its PCNE wording in the form’s free-text field. *Why:* PCNE separates the problem from its cause, and the form’s boxes are mostly causes — “effect not optimal” caused by a low dose should tick “dose too low”, not also “ineffective therapy”. The trainee can adjust the boxes before export.

**Cipolle (teaching view).** A mapping, for teaching: PCNE and Cipolle, Strand and Morley classify drug-related problems differently, and the two are not equivalent. The PCNE code is the record. Each cause gives a category, or none; some depend on the problem’s domain (P1 effectiveness, P2 safety, P3 other). When several causes give categories, the first in Cipolle’s order of assessment wins (indication → effectiveness → safety → adherence). With no category from the causes, the problem’s own category is used.

## Choices for you to confirm (⚑)

- **C4.1** Duration of treatment too short → **Dose too low**. Cipolle counts a wrong duration under dosage. The alternative is "other".
- **C4.2** Duration of treatment too long → **Dose too high**. As C4.1. The alternative is "other".
- **C6.2** Drug under-administered by a health professional → **Dose too low**. Under-administered: the patient received less than prescribed.
- **C6.3** Drug over-administered by a health professional → **Dose too high**. Over-administered: the patient received more than prescribed.
- **C7.2** Patient uses/takes more drug than prescribed → **Non-adherence**. Taking more than prescribed. The alternative is "dose too high".
- **C7.3** Patient abuses drug (unregulated overuse) → **Unnecessary medication**. Cipolle files addiction and recreational use under unnecessary drug therapy. The alternative is "non-adherence".
- **C7.5** Patient takes food that interacts → **Drug interaction**. A food–drug interaction.
- **C7.9** Patient physically unable to use drug/form as directed → **Non-adherence**. Cipolle counts inability to use the drug under non-adherence.
- **C7.10** Patient unable to understand instructions properly → **Non-adherence**. As C7.9.

| Code | PCNE V9.1 wording | Department form box | Cipolle category | Why |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| **P1** | **Treatment effectiveness** | | | |
| P1.1 | No effect of drug treatment despite correct use | Ineffective therapy | Ineffective drug |  |
| P1.2 | Effect of drug treatment not optimal | Ineffective therapy | Ineffective drug | Form: Effect not optimal. Used only when no cause gives a more specific box (a low dose ticks "dose too low" instead). Cipolle: Used when no cause decides (a low dose makes it "dosage too low"). |
| P1.3 | Untreated symptoms or indication | Need for additional therapy | Needs additional drug therapy |  |
| **P2** | **Treatment safety** | | | |
| P2.1 | Adverse drug event (possibly) occurring | Adverse drug reaction | Adverse drug reaction | Form: Used only when no cause gives a more specific box (a dose too high or an interaction is ticked instead). Cipolle: Used when no cause decides (a dose too high makes it "dosage too high"). |
| **P3** | **Other** | | | |
| P3.1 | Unnecessary drug-treatment | Unnecessary medication | Unnecessary drug therapy |  |
| P3.2 | Unclear problem/complaint. Further clarification necessary (please use as escape only) | Other | *no equivalent* | Form: An unclear problem has no box. |

## Causes

| Code | PCNE V9.1 wording | Department form box | Cipolle category | Why |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| **C1** | **Drug selection** | | | |
| C1.1 | Inappropriate drug according to guidelines/formulary | Other | P1: Ineffective drug; P2: Adverse drug reaction; P3: Unnecessary drug therapy | Form: Says the drug is inappropriate, not what kind of problem follows: the problem’s box is ticked too, and this wording goes under "other". Cipolle: A more effective drug exists → ineffective drug; a drug unsafe for this patient → adverse drug reaction; a drug without a place in the guidelines → unnecessary drug therapy. |
| C1.2 | No indication for drug | Unnecessary medication | Unnecessary drug therapy |  |
| C1.3 | Inappropriate combination of drugs, or drugs and herbal medications, or drugs and dietary supplements | Drug interaction | P1: Dosage too low; P2: Adverse drug reaction; P3: *no equivalent* | Cipolle: An interaction that lowers the effect → dosage too low; one that harms → adverse drug reaction (Cipolle files a level raised by an interaction under dosage too high, which the codes cannot tell apart). |
| C1.4 | Inappropriate duplication of therapeutic group or active ingredient | Unnecessary medication | Unnecessary drug therapy | Form: A duplicate drug is an unnecessary one. |
| C1.5 | No or incomplete drug treatment in spite of existing indication | Need for additional therapy | Needs additional drug therapy |  |
